How recording works
With a time chosen, history is recorded for that time and then stops by itself.
A row is recorded whenever the radio state changes and once a minute, on this device.
It uses the ongoing notification and keeps recording with the screen off or locked, reading the cells about every 10 seconds (this uses battery).
Stop in the ongoing notification stops it too.

Carrier composition\nWith the carrier composition set to Automatic in Settings, it is recorded too.\nWhile recording, Android\'s setting nr_nsa_tracking_screen_off_mode is set to 2 through Shizuku and put back afterwards, so that changes are reported with the screen off (this uses battery).

Generate traffic\nWith Generate traffic on in Settings, a little data is downloaded over the data SIM at the Traffic interval (2 seconds at first) while recording, from a speed-test server (speed.cloudflare.com).\nThe time to each answer and the requests left unanswered are recorded too (this uses mobile data).
Not recorded, not sent\nNothing is sent.\nPhone numbers and SIM identifiers are not recorded.

NR is connected, confirmed by Android (PhysicalChannelConfig or the cell list). The NR column shows the frequency class (Sub-6, Refarmed, mmWave; several in use are listed together, such as \"Sub-6 + Refarmed\"), or \"connected\" if unknown. NSA or SA appears in the Network column
In a 5G area, but NR has not been added (idle, or data over LTE only)
Hints such as a 5G icon exist, but an NR connection cannot be confirmed
Not registered on the network: no service, radio off, airplane mode, etc.
4G+ means LTE CA. 5G+ means NR is connected and meets the carrier\'s conditions (NR band, total NR bandwidth, mmWave, etc.). The + is dropped while idle
NR at 3.6 GHz and above (n77, n78, n79); outside Japan, 3.3 GHz and above
NR at 24 GHz and above (n257, n258, n261, etc.)
On Japanese networks, NR below 3.6 GHz (n28, n3, n40, n41, etc.): spectrum originally used for LTE and refarmed for 5G
Calculated because it is not reported. SCC RSSI is RSRP − RSRQ + 10·log₁₀(resource blocks in the bandwidth)

TA (timing advance) is how much earlier the phone sends, a clue to the distance from the cell. The value is shown as reported and not converted to a distance. For 4G it is the standard\'s step count. For 5G it is a value Android passes as microseconds, but the documents disagree on its unit and it has not been confirmed. On the Pixel 10a some 4G values came to tens of kilometres inside Tokyo and the 5G value hardly changed from cell to cell, so a distance would mislead.
Android\'s bandwidth list contained a single value, assumed to be this cell\'s

Estimated downlink peak, computed from assumed values the device does not report; not an exact figure from the standards tables, and real speeds are usually a fraction of it. Assumes 256QAM; 4×4 MIMO at 1 GHz and above except mmWave, 2×2 below and for mmWave; NR subcarrier spacing of 30 kHz for TDD and 15 kHz for FDD (120 kHz for mmWave); and 75% of TDD time on the downlink. LTE scales the 20 MHz, 4-layer peak (391.7 Mbit/s) by resource blocks and layers, an approximation
NR bandwidth taken as what remains of the reported bandwidth list after the LTE carriers
The frequency alone does not identify the band, so the band Android reported earlier is shown
Possible bands: the frequency alone does not identify the band, and none was reported

Shizuku\nAfter a reboot, start Shizuku; saved carrier names are then restored automatically.\nShizuku is used to change carrier names and for the experimental features.

Ongoing notification
It stops updating its display while the screen is off.
With a time chosen for recording history (in History), it keeps recording for that time with the screen off or locked.
After a reboot, it resumes when you open the app.

Generate traffic
It runs while the bands screen is open or history is being recorded.
While history is being recorded, it continues even with the screen closed or off.
It downloads 1 KB at the Traffic interval from a speed-test server (speed.cloudflare.com) over the data SIM's mobile network, even on Wi-Fi.
About 3 KB each time with the connection set-up.
It uses mobile data and battery.
A shorter interval catches shorter stalls but keeps the modem from resting, so it uses more battery (at 2 seconds the radio was active 74 percent of 17 hours with the screen off).
No device information is sent.
Experimental features\nThey rely on Android internals and may stop working after an Android update.

A SIM card is a physical SIM; with a down arrow, an eSIM (as in Android\'s settings). The SIM used for data has a dark SIM icon and number; the other SIM\'s are light. The download icon and amount at the right of the header are what Generate traffic (Settings) has received (\"Waiting\" while waiting for mobile data, a red \"No answer\" when nothing answers)
